newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs steady to lower, NYMEX gives support.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs steady to lower, NYMEX gives support.

text.p: U.S. liquefied petroleum gas prices were stable on Tuesday in quiet midday trade that found support in NYMEX crude oil and natgas futures, players said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane traded at 38.125 cents a gallon, unchanged from Monday.
Conway, Kansas, hub material also got hit at 37.00 cents and remained in Monday's 36.75/37.00 cent range.
"There is not any real big news out there. Crude is supporting the market a bit and a little of natural gas," said one Houston broker.
NYMEX natgas futures were high amid shortcovering and talk of firmer cash prices. May crude was up on strength in heating oil.

Conway natural gasoline, however, drifted down following news that NCRA, one of the hub's largest buyers of the material, will begin a month-long turnaround at its Mcpherson, Kansas, refinery April 1.
Conway natural gasoline was at 46.75/47.00 cents, a quarter cents below Monday. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
